nf2e7d5fd209.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Gandhi's settlements and ashrams?
o: Sabarmati Ashram was established before Tolstoy Farm
nf2e7d5fd209.x: Sabarmati Ashram came in 1917, after Tolstoy Farm (1910); the order is Phoenix (1904), Tolstoy Farm (1910), Sabarmati (1917), Sevagram (1936).

ne042080894d.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Gandhian economic approach?
o: It directs production primarily toward profit maximisation
ne042080894d.x: Gandhi wanted production directed toward need, not profit; a non-violent economy needs decentralisation and self-reliance.

new.s: Before going to London, Gandhi studied at which college?
new.x: Gandhi studied at Samaldas College, Bhavnagar, before studying law at the Inner Temple, London.

new.s: Gandhi studied law in London during:
new.x: Gandhi studied law at the Inner Temple, London, from 1888 to 1891.

new.s: After returning from London, Gandhi's unsuccessful legal practice was at:
new.x: His legal practice at Rajkot and Bombay did not succeed; in 1893 he went to South Africa.

new.s: The Natal Indian Congress was founded by Gandhi in:
new.x: Gandhi founded the Natal Indian Congress in 1894.

new.s: The Great March of 1913 in South Africa was mainly against:
new.x: The 1913 Great March opposed the £3 poll tax and the invalidation of Indian marriages; miners and indentured workers joined.

new.s: In South Africa, Gandhi worked as a compounder in which hospital as part of his 'Seva Dharma'?
new.x: He adopted Seva Dharma by working as a compounder in Rustomji's charity hospital and serving the Boer War wounded.

new.s: Gandhi stayed in South Africa for about:
new.x: Gandhi was in South Africa from 1893 to 1914, about 21 years.

new.s: Tolstoy Farm near Johannesburg was set up by Gandhi with the help of:
new.x: Tolstoy Farm (1910) was set up with Hermann Kallenbach as a cooperative settlement for satyagrahis and their families.

new.s: Gandhi's first ashram in India was:
new.x: Kochrab Ashram, Ahmedabad (1915) was his first ashram in India; Sabarmati followed in 1917.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Tolstoy Farm:
1. It was set up near Johannesburg in 1910.
2. The Indian National Congress helped to found it.
new.x: Tolstoy Farm was set up near Johannesburg in 1910; the INC had no role in it.

new.s: Gandhi took the idea of the right to break unjust laws from:
new.x: Thoreau's Civil Disobedience gave Gandhi the right to break unjust laws.

new.s: Who gave Gandhi a copy of Unto This Last in 1904?
new.x: Henry Polak gave Gandhi Unto This Last in 1904; it influenced him most.

new.s: Among the five Jain vows that influenced Gandhi, which was added by Mahavira?
new.x: The first four vows come from Parshvanatha; brahmacharya was added by Mahavira.

new.s: Which pair of book and author, as an influence on Gandhi, is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: The Kingdom of God is Within You – John Ruskin
new.x: The Kingdom of God is Within You was written by Leo Tolstoy, not Ruskin.

new.s: Hind Swaraj was banned in 1910 by the:
new.x: Hind Swaraj was banned by the Bombay Government in 1910.

new.s: Gandhi wrote Hind Swaraj aboard the ship:
new.x: Hind Swaraj was written in 1909 aboard the Kildonan Castle, from London to South Africa.

new.s: The English version of Hind Swaraj was translated by:
new.x: Gandhi translated Hind Swaraj into English himself, to get round the ban.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Hind Swaraj?
new.x: Hind Swaraj was against industrialisation and modern civilisation, stressing self-reliance and rural life.

new.s: Young India, edited by Gandhi from 1919, was published in:
new.x: Young India was an English weekly.

new.s: Harijan, started by Gandhi in 1933, was a:
new.x: Harijan was a 1933 English weekly; Harijan Bandhu was Gujarati and Harijan Sevak Hindi.

new.s: Anasakti Yoga by Gandhi is a Gujarati rendering, with commentary, of the:
new.x: Anasakti Yoga is Gandhi's Gujarati rendering of the Gita with commentary.

new.s: The Collected Works of Mahatma Gandhi in English run to:
new.x: The Collected Works run to 100 volumes, published by the Publications Division.

new.s: Gandhi's autobiography was first serialised in:
new.x: Navajivan was Gandhi's Gujarati paper in which his autobiography was serialised.

new.s: Which pair of paper and person is correctly matched?
new.x: Mook Nayak was Ambedkar's paper; Comrade was Muhammad Ali's and Vande Mataram Aurobindo's.

new.s: On his return to India on 9 January 1915, Gandhi landed at:
new.x: Gandhi landed at Bombay on 9 January 1915.

new.s: Gandhi received the Kaisar-i-Hind gold medal in 1915 for his:
o: Recruitment drive in the First World War
new.x: The Kaisar-i-Hind gold medal (1915) was given for his ambulance work in South Africa.

new.s: Gandhi's first hunger strike in India was during the:
new.x: Ahmedabad 1918 (mill wages) was the first hunger strike; Champaran was civil disobedience and Kheda non-cooperation.

new.s: The title 'Mahatma' was given to Gandhi by:
new.x: Rabindranath Tagore called Gandhi 'Mahatma' in 1914.

new.s: Subhas Chandra Bose called Gandhi 'Father of the Nation' in:
new.x: Bose called Gandhi Father of the Nation on Azad Hind radio, Singapore, on 6 July 1944.

new.s: Gandhi returned the Kaisar-i-Hind gold medal in 1920 in connection with the:
new.x: He returned the medal in 1920 during the Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.

new.s: In September 2026, AP Assembly Speaker Ch. Ayyanna Patrudu visited which station linked to Gandhi?
new.x: On 14 September 2026 he visited Pietermaritzburg station and the Gandhi Memorial in KwaZulu-Natal.

new.s: The Telugu book Agamya Gamyaalu by Mukunda Ramarao traces:
o: Andhra indentured migrants to South Africa
new.x: Agamya Gamyaalu (February 2026) traces Andhra indentured migrants to South Africa.

new.s: Gandhi described ahimsa as a quality of the:
new.x: Gandhi held ahimsa, in thought, word and deed, to be a quality of the brave, not the weak.

new.s: In Gandhian thought, truth is described as:
new.x: Gandhi described truth as reality: existence, consciousness and bliss.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Gandhi's truth and ahimsa:
1. Truth is the end and non-violence the means.
2. 'Truth is God' was his earlier formulation.
3. Ahimsa is to be practised in thought, word and deed.
new.x: 'God is Truth' came first and 'Truth is God' later, so statement 2 is wrong.

new.s: According to Gandhi, the first step of satyagraha was:
new.x: Fasting, the 'Fire Arrow', was the first step; strike was the last.

new.s: The driving force of satyagraha, according to Gandhi, is:
new.x: Suffering is the driving force of satyagraha; its aim is not to defeat the enemy.

new.s: Which form of satyagraha marked the Rowlatt Satyagraha of 1919?
new.x: The Rowlatt Satyagraha of 1919 used hartal and was the first all-India mass movement.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about satyagraha?
o: Its aim is to defeat the enemy
It was born in 1906 in the Transvaal
new.x: The aim of satyagraha is not to defeat the enemy; suffering is its driving force.

new.s: According to Gandhi, real swaraj lies in the capacity of all to:
new.x: Gandhi said real swaraj is the capacity of all to resist authority when it is abused.

new.s: The key suggestion of Gandhi's politics for governance was:
new.x: Gandhi's politics proposed decentralisation through village panchayats, with no place for authority.

new.s: 'Means are after all everything.' Gandhi completes it as:
o: As the means so the end
new.x: Gandhi said, 'Means are after all everything. As the means so the end.'

new.s: Which of the following is included in Gandhi's concept of Swaraj?
new.x: Swaraj meant self-rule and self-control, not only political freedom.

new.s: The Jain thinker who influenced Gandhi was:
new.x: Gandhi was influenced by Jainism in Gujarat, notably by the Jain thinker Raychandbhai.

new.s: For Gandhi, the essence of Christ's teaching lay in the:
new.x: Gandhi saw the Sermon on the Mount as the essence of Christ's teaching.

new.s: Which pair of influence and work is correctly matched?
o: Ruskin – The Kingdom of God is Within You
new.x: Thoreau wrote Civil Disobedience; Ruskin wrote Unto This Last and Tolstoy The Kingdom of God is Within You.

new.s: Gandhi described the State as:
o: The march of God on earth
new.x: Gandhi, a philosophical anarchist, called the State violence in concentrated form.

new.s: Unlike Marxism, the method of Gandhism is:
new.x: Gandhism relies on non-violence and change of heart; Marxism on class struggle and revolution.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT Gandhian?
new.x: Class dictatorship is not Gandhian; trusteeship, Sarvodaya and means-ends purity are his core values.

new.s: In 2026, Gandhian non-violence was linked to the Baltic Way and the:
new.x: Gandhian non-violence was linked to the Baltic Way and the Singing Revolution of Baltic re-independence (1991).

new.s: The term 'Gandhian Innovation' was coined by:
new.x: Gandhian Innovation (more from less for more people) was coined by Prof. Prahlad and R.A. Mashelkar.

new.s: Gandhi's Gujarati retelling of Unto This Last, titled 'Sarvodaya', appeared in:
new.x: Gandhi's Gujarati retelling 'Sarvodaya' of Ruskin's Unto This Last appeared in 1908.

new.s: Gandhi's booklet Constructive Programme was published in:
new.x: Constructive Programme was a 1941 booklet by Gandhi.

new.s: Tolstoy took the term 'bread labour' from:
new.x: Tolstoy took the term bread labour from T.M. Bondaref; Gandhi drew it from Tolstoy and Ruskin.

new.s: Gandhi linked the idea of bread labour to the Gita's concept of:
new.x: Gandhi linked bread labour to the Gita's yajna.

new.s: From which of the following did Gandhi NOT draw his idea of bread labour?
new.x: Thoreau gave civil disobedience, not bread labour.

new.s: Which of the following statements about Gandhian economy is NOT correct?
o: Gandhi opposed mechanisation even in the USA
Agriculture and village industries get priority
Production should be for need, not profit
new.x: Gandhi held each economy depends on its climate, land and people, so he did not oppose mechanisation in the USA.

new.s: According to Gandhi, a country's economy should be defined by its:
o: Climate, land and the nature of its citizens
new.x: Gandhi held each economy should fit its climate, land and the nature of its citizens.

new.s: The idea of trusteeship is linked by Gandhi to:
new.x: Trusteeship is linked to South Africa, 1903, when he had a law firm at Johannesburg.

new.s: The Ahmedabad Mill Strike of 1918 ended with a wage rise of:
new.x: Gandhi's fast in the 1918 Ahmedabad Mill Strike won a 35% wage rise.

new.s: The 'Practical Trusteeship Formula' was drafted by:
new.x: Narhari Parikh and Kishorelal Mashruwala drafted it while Gandhi was held at Aga Khan Palace; M.L. Dantwala refined it.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Gandhian trusteeship:
1. It applied to both capitalists and zamindars.
2. The Textile Labour Association of 1920 used arbitration.
new.x: Trusteeship covered capitalists and zamindars, and the Textile Labour Association (1920) used arbitration and non-violence.

new.s: The 'Gandhian Plan' was drafted by:
new.x: Shriman Narayan Aggarwal drafted the Gandhian Plan; JP drafted the Sarvodaya Plan.

new.s: The Gandhian Constitution for Free India (1946) was written by:
new.x: Shriman Narayan Aggarwal wrote it in 1946, with Gandhi's foreword.

new.s: Sarvodaya Day is observed on:
new.x: Sarvodaya Day is observed on 30 January.

new.s: Under Bhoodan, landlords were asked to gift at least ____ of their land.
new.x: Vinoba asked landlords to gift at least one-sixth of their land.

new.s: Who organised the Sarvodaya Samaj?
new.x: Vinoba Bhave made Sarvodaya the cornerstone and organised the Sarvodaya Samaj.

new.s: Prakasam's Khadi Development Centre that got Rs 10,000 from the AISA was at:
new.x: The centre at Guravareddypalem (Guntur) got Rs 10,000 from the All India Spinners' Association.

new.s: Which pair of body and year is INCORRECTLY matched?
new.x: The All India Village Industries Association dates from 1934; 1925 is the Spinners' Association.

new.s: Which Article of the Constitution directs the State to promote cottage industries?
new.x: Article 43 covers cottage industries; 40 panchayats and 47 prohibition.

new.s: Gandhi's rural development approach is known as:
new.x: Gandhi's approach to rural development was Samagra Gramseva.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT an item of Gandhi's constructive programme?
new.x: Constructive programme items included khadi, prohibition, removal of untouchability, national schools, Hindu-Muslim unity and village panchayats.
